ai.mechanism: Evidence shows only an outflow: 3,499,995 USDC left contract 0x367c42a6f261ec54ffbecf5f41c226be12a3dca0, removing 95.2% of its balance. The packet contains no caller privilege data, no failed access check, no initialisation event, no price source and no callback pattern, so no exploit mechanism can be named.
ai.lossBearer: Undetermined. Only the drained contract 0x367c42a6f261ec54ffbecf5f41c226be12a3dca0 is shown as losing funds; no integrators or downstream exposed parties are listed.
ai.narrative: A single Ethereum transaction moved 3,499,995 USDC (about $3.5m) out of one contract, taking roughly 95% of what it held. That is the entire story the data tells. Large near-total sweeps are exactly what a treasury consolidation, a bridge settlement or a contract migration look like, and the packet gives nothing to separate those from theft: no protocol name, no instrument, no privileged-caller anomaly, no integrator with visible exposure. Until someone can show the mover lacked authority, or show a counterparty that actually eats the loss, this is an unexplained transfer, not a confirmed exploit.
